title: Making tricky plurals: words ending in y, f, and hissing sounds
canonical_examples_source: Standard T&T/UK primary spelling rules; plurals self-verified. Format ref: bank uk-ks2-2024-gps (KS2 GPS spelling).

blocks.content: You are helping Aunty label the jars in her parlour: babies' biscuits, mango boxes, sweet shelves. Most words become plural by just adding -s: one book, two books. But some are tricky. Let's learn three little tricks so every label is right. Quick words: consonant means letters like b, c, d that make sounds where you stop the air. hissing sounds means sounds made with sharp air like s, sh, ch, and x.
Trick 1 — When a word ends in a consonant then y, change the y to i and add es.

steps: 'baby' ends in a consonant (b) then y.

blocks.explain: 'city' ends in a consonant (t) then y, so change y to i and add es: cities.
blocks.rule: If a word ends in a consonant then y, change the y to i and add es.

blocks.content: Trick 2 — When a word ends in f or fe, change the f to v and add es.

blocks.question: What is the plural of 'leaf'?
blocks.explain: 'leaf' ends in f, so change the f to v and add es: leaves.
blocks.rule: If a word ends in f or fe, change the f to v and add es.

blocks.content: Trick 3 — When a word ends in a hissing sound (s, x, ch, or sh), add es.

blocks.explain: 'bus' ends in the hissing sound s, so add es: buses.
blocks.rule: If a word ends in s, x, ch or sh, add es to make it plural.

blocks.question: Aunty writes 'potatos' on a label. But the real plural of 'potato' is 'potatoes'. Which of these is the BEST reason her first spelling was wrong?
options: 'potato' ends in o, a hissing-style ending, so it takes es — like the -es trick, not just -s
'potato' ends in a consonant then y, so change y to i
'potato' ends in f, so change f to v
blocks.explain: 'potato' does not end in y or f, so Tricks 1 and 2 do not fit. It ends in o, which behaves like the hissing group and takes es: potatoes. The key skill is choosing WHICH trick fits before you spell.
blocks.rule: Before making a plural, decide which ending the word has, then apply the matching trick.
blocks.principle: A plural rule only applies when the word's ending matches it; you must first identify the ending.
canonical_solution: 'potato' ends in o, not y and not f.
Tricks 1 (y to i) and 2 (f to v) do not apply.
Words like potato/tomato/hero take es: potatoes.
So the reason is: it needs es, like the -es group, not a plain -s.

rubric.look_for: checks the actual ending of 'potato' (o), not a guessed trick
rules OUT the y and f tricks because the ending does not match
states that the right trick depends on the word's ending

misconceptions.coach: 'potato' has no y before the end. The y trick only fits words like baby or city.
Not yet — some endings need es. Look at the last letters first.

blocks.content: Aunty's labels are perfect now. Three tricks: consonant + y turns to ies, f turns to ves, and hissing sounds add es — and always check the ending first to pick the right one. Time to practise!
